description:
## Description

Adds Twig templates language support as en extra.

Explanation for the tools choices:
- Linter/formatter: Twigcs and Twig-cs-fixer both follow the [coding standards](https://twig.symfony.com/doc/3.x/coding_standards.html) recommended by the Symfony Project, maintainers of Twig.
- LSP: I don't know it Twiggy is considered a standard in the community. I picked it because it's the only server specific to Twig. The other options are HTML servers that also include support for several templates languages. I've been using it for a while and it works fine. It adds much needed snippets (Twig syntax involves tags that are difficult to type on most keyboards) and does not conflict with Twigcs diagnostics.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) guidelines.

comments.body: You could remove that, since it's not necessary because the LSP servers that are defined in `nvim-lspconfig` plugin spec get automatically resolved and installed. That will also give you the green light in the current test that's failing.

```suggestion
        twiggy_language_server = {
```
should do it because it doesn't contain any invalid string characters to be enclosed in square brackets. Underscores are valid in strings.

You should at least provide the recommended root by [nvim-lspconfig](https://github.com/neovim/nvim-lspconfig/blob/b4d65bce97795438ab6e1974b3672c17a4865e3c/lua/lspconfig/configs/twiggy_language_server.lua#L7). I've no idea if more are needed, since I'm not familiar with php. It's up to you.
I mean only the line `"twiggy-language-server",` on line 13, not everything else. I should have used a Github suggestion, sorry about that.

I will if it's necessary to make the check pass, but this isn't really a good idea.

Using Composer means your project uses PHP, but it does not mean your project uses Twig, far from it actually. There are multiple other template languages available, and even the possibility to not use any since PHP itself is a template language (although quite limited).

I don't want to recommend Twig extra to any PHP developer if I can avoid it.
At first, I thought it was "twiggy-language-server" and not "twiggy_language_server", I forgot to remove the brackets afterwards. :smile:
